title: Veterans' Mental Health Crisis Severity Annotation: Do LLMs Agree More Than Human Experts?
abstract: arXiv:2611.10048v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) offer a scalable approach for annotating mental health and crisis-related social media content, but their reliability in safety-critical tasks remains unclear. This study evaluates LLM-based crisis-severity annotation of veteran-related social media posts against annotations from eight Veteran Subject Matter Experts (SMEs). Using 149 tweets and five severity categories, we evaluate 15 open-source and 10 proprietary LLMs across eight prompt variants, examining annotation performance, inter-model agreement, prompt sensitivity, and high-severity crisis detection. Human reviewers showed higher ordinal than nominal agreement ({\alpha} = 0.494), indicating that disagreements often occurred between neighboring severity levels. translated_title: 退伍军人心理健康危机严重程度标注：大语言模型比人类专家更具一致性吗？
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）为心理健康和危机相关社交媒体内容的标注提供了一种可扩展的方法，但其在安全关键任务中的可靠性仍不明确。本研究将基于LLM的退伍军人相关社交媒体帖子的危机严重程度标注，与八位退伍军人领域专家（SME）的标注进行了对比评估。研究使用149条推文和五个严重程度类别，在八种提示词变体下评估了15个开源模型和10个专有LLM，考察了标注性能、模型间一致性、提示敏感性以及高严重度危机检测能力。人类评审者表现出更高的序数一致性而非名义一致性（α = 0.494），表明分歧常常发生在相邻的严重程度级别之间。相比之下，选定的LLM表现出显著更高的模型间一致性，在基线提示下序数一致性（α）达到0.8336。专有模型总体（原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本研究对比了大语言模型与八位退伍军人专家对社交媒体帖子危机严重程度的标注，发现选定的LLM之间的一致性显著更高（序数α达0.8336），而人类专家一致性较低（α=0.494）且分歧多发生在相邻严重程度级别之间。
en_tdlr: Comparing LLM-based crisis-severity annotation of veteran-related social media posts with eight human subject matter experts, this study finds that selected LLMs achieve substantially higher inter-model agreement (ordinal α up to 0.8336) than human experts (α = 0.494), whose disagreements mainly occur between adjacent severity levels.
